en.title: Minimum Operations Sorting Proper Substrings
en.description:
Each operation chooses any non-empty proper substring (not the whole string) and sorts its characters in ascending order. Find the minimum number of operations needed to sort the whole string in ascending order.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, examples, and judging.
en.input: A single line containing a lowercase string of length 3..100000.
en.explanation: Example 1: the first character z is the unique maximum and the last character a is the unique minimum, so 3 operations are needed: sort the first 5, the last 5, and the first 5 characters in turn. Example 2: already sorted, 0 operations. Example 3: the last c is already the maximum, so sorting the first two characters ba is enough, 1 operation.
hints: An already sorted string needs 0. If the first character is the global minimum or the last character is the global maximum, sorting the rest takes only 1. Otherwise, if the first character is the unique maximum and the last character is the unique minimum, 3 are needed; in all other cases, 2.
